newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Australian state to ban smoking in restaurants.
newsitem.headline: Australian state to ban smoking in restaurants.

text.p: South Australia state said on Tuesday it hoped to protect captive diners from unwanted nicotine by banning smoking in restaurants and other public eating places.
Health minister Michael Armitage said the state government would ban smoking in all enclosed eating areas of restaurants, hotels, shopping malls and cafes from 1999.

Armitage said restaurant owners in the state, renowned for the quality of its food, had complained of sending their chefs out to markets in the early morning hours to get the best produce only to have it ruined by a table of smokers.
"Diners in enclosed eating areas are 'captive audiences', there is little they can do to avoid tobacco smoke from a nearby table," he said, announcing the move.

The move is a first for the six Australian states, although the Australian Capital Territory which includes Australia's capital city Canberra, already has a ban on smoking on all restaurants and hotels.
